correctness.rationale: Classification into translations and reflections (unique at rank two or above) and separate handling of empty/singletons give exhaustive disjoint cases. Translation index is one plus longest selected residue-strand run; reflection index two iff no pair or fixed point selected. This yields the exact cumulative polynomial; hockey-stick and reflection-pair multiplicity give rank/total formulas. Reflection contributions are exponentially smaller than translation and independent fair bits give matching logarithmic run bounds. Standalone direct partial-map composition checked all ranks and powers for chain sizes one through nine, including boundary cases. Finite tests do not replace infinite proof.

value.rationale: Domain rank and nilpotency index are intrinsic, distinct semigroup-element invariants. A full joint distribution for every chain size and index is a natural missing refinement of classical partial-isometry enumeration, distinguishing bounded-index reflections from arbitrarily long translation chains; it also yields the nontrivial nilpotent density one-third and logarithmic typical depth. This is not merely a new label, an arbitrary small slice, or known-table recomputation. The related existing contraction stabilization limit applies to different maps and does not imply the joint law.
